findings.evidence: Folding/Eigenspaces.lean:45 `def typeDGraphSplit : (((Unit ⊕ (I ⊕ I)) → A) × A) ≃ₗ[A] ((Option I ⊕ Option I) → A)`. Its docstring at :22-23 says it retains the scalar factors needed to restrict skew-adjoint endomorphisms to the fixed space. Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Option.lean:243 `def optionSubtypeNe`.
findings.fix: Build these four matrices from `typeDGraphSplit` and its inverse (via `LinearMap.toMatrix'` on the two components), re-indexed by `Equiv.optionSubtypeNe c : Option {b // b ≠ c} ≃ I`. Alternatively state the whole development for `Option I` with `none` and get the numbered case through `finSuccEquivLast`.
findings.issue: `typeDGraphInclusion`, `typeDGraphAntiInclusion`, `typeDGraphProjection` and `typeDGraphAntiProjection` are a second copy of the existing split `TauCeti.typeDGraphSplit`. That split already sends (fixed coordinates, anti-fixed scalar) to the type-D coordinates, with the 1/2 averaging inverse. The only difference here is indexing by `{i // i ≠ c}` instead of `Option I` with `none`.

findings.evidence: Folding/Eigenspaces.lean:165 `theorem typeDGraphSplit_bilin : (JD (Option I) A).toBilin' (typeDGraphSplit I A p) (typeDGraphSplit I A q) = (JB I A).toBilin' p.1 q.1 - 2 * p.2 * q.2`.
findings.fix: Derive all three from `typeDGraphSplit_bilin` (or from `typeDGraphSplitIsometry`) through `Matrix.toBilin'` once the matrices are defined from the split.
findings.issue: `typeDGraphInclusion_gram`, `typeDGraphInclusion_gram_antiInclusion` and `typeDGraphAntiInclusion_gram` are the matrix form of `typeDGraphSplit_bilin`, which already shows the type-D form splits as `JB` plus a line of norm −2. Each is re-proved by its own coordinate case split.

findings.evidence: Folding/Eigenspaces.lean:57-71 (left_inv and right_inv of `typeDGraphSplit`) and :117 `typeDGraphSplit_graphIndex`, which shows the pair swap acts as `(x,t) ↦ (x,-t)` in the split coordinates.
findings.fix: Once the matrices are defined from `typeDGraphSplit`, obtain these from `LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply` and `apply_symm_apply` and from `typeDGraphSplit_graphIndex`, instead of keeping a parallel set of lemmas.
findings.issue: `typeDGraphProjection_mul_inclusion`, `typeDGraphAntiProjection_mul_antiInclusion`, the two cross-term lemmas and `typeDGraphInclusion_mul_projection_add` are the two inverse laws of `typeDGraphSplit`. `typeDGraphMatrix_mul_inclusion` and `typeDGraphMatrix_mul_antiInclusion` restate `typeDGraphSplit_graphIndex`. All of these are re-proved by separate case splits.

summary: Coordinates.lean rebuilds, as matrices, the split of the type-D graph involution that `typeDGraphSplit` in TypeD/Folding/Eigenspaces.lean already provides, together with its Gram and inverse lemmas. The rest (type-B reindexing, the fixed-algebra equivalence) is new and reuses Mathlib.
